learning_outcomes.text: Know, understand and apply the concepts of computational fluid mechanics science and technology to adapt to new situations.
Perform measurements, calculations, studies and reports on the operating parameters of different types of fluid installations.
Ability to work in a multilingual environment.
Adopt a responsible, orderly attitude to work and be willing to learn the concepts of numerical solution of fluid dynamic problems, considering the challenge that continuous training will pose.
Apply strategies typical of the scientific methodology: analyze the problematic situation qualitatively and quantitatively, propose hypotheses and solutions to solve fluid mechanics problems.
Knowledge and skills to apply computer-aided graphic engineering techniques.
Applied knowledge of the fundamentals of fluid-mechanical systems and machines.

syllabus_topics: Philosophy and field of application of computational fluid dynamics.
Equations governing the flow: Continuity, momentum, and energy.
Mathematical considerations of differential equations: Generalities. Hyperbolic, parabolic, and elliptic differential equations. Simplifications of the Navier-Stokes equation.

Preliminary discretization techniques: Discretization. Approximation of derivatives. Accuracy of the discretization process. Implicit and explicit approximation. Theoretical framework: convergence, stability, accuracy of the solution.
Brief notes on similarity theory: Physical meaning of dimensionless numbers.
Turbulent flow: Reynolds time-averaged equations. Turbulent kinetic energy equation models. Boundary layer.

Basic computational methods applied to incompressible flow: Solution of the transport equation. Methods for solving the stream function. Boundary conditions. Methods for solving the pressure-velocity equation.
Basic computational methods applied to compressible flow: Methods for the numerical treatment of shock waves.
Mesh generation and appropriate equation transformations.
Multiphase flow: Eulerian and Lagrangian approximation. VOF (Volume of Fluid) method.
User-level learning of a commercial computational fluid dynamics code.
Application of theoretical concepts in practical computer simulation exercises of real fluid mechanics problems. Comparison of laboratory testing vs. simulation.

assessment_methods.method: Individual assignments (questions and small problems deliverables)

assessment_rules: For continuous assessment, 80% attendance to in-person hours is required to be graded; otherwise, the student will be marked as "not presented". Students who, at the beginning of the course, justify any of the reasons stated in Article 43.1.c of the EHU/UPV regulations may obtain 100% of the grade through a theoretical-practical exam. For extraordinary examination, students who participated in continuous assessment and did not pass will take a complementary final test. Students who did not participate in continuous assessment can obtain 100% of the grade through a theoretical-practical exam, requiring contact with the professor at least one month prior.
